issues.t: Head gasket and cam seal leaks on the 2.4L
issues.sym: Oil leaking from the engine, coolant loss, overheating, white smoke, or oil and coolant mixing. Some cars stall and won't restart once it gets bad.
issues.why: The original head gasket on the 2.4L four-cylinder can fail, sometimes more than once, and the camshaft seals can push out. Chrysler issued service bulletins for an improved multi-layer steel gasket and for cam seal retention.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats or the oil looks milky. Ask the shop to use the updated gasket and to check the cam seals during the repair.

issues.t: Automatic transmission shifts erratically or drops out of gear
issues.sym: Sudden downshifts, slipping or dropping gears, hesitation or lurching when put in Drive, getting stuck in one gear, or the transmission quitting at highway speed.
issues.why: The electronically controlled 4-speed automatic depends on its computer and sensors; faulty controls and internal wear both cause erratic shifting.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition, then have codes read. Fix any sensor or computer faults before agreeing to a rebuild.

issues.t: Engine stalls while driving or when slowing down
issues.sym: The engine dies at stops, when slowing for a turn or while cruising, and may not restart until it cools down.
issues.why: A failing crankshaft position sensor or its wiring is a common cause on these cars. Many owners replaced fuel pumps and ignition parts without curing it.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the crank sensor and its wiring tested, especially if the stall happens when the engine is hot, before replacing the fuel pump.

issues.t: No-start or stalling from broken wiring
issues.sym: The car cranks but won't start, stalls, or stumbles when accelerating. Some cars won't start after rain or a wash, or only run when wires near the ignition switch are moved.
issues.why: Wires in the engine and ignition harness can break or corrode over time, interrupting signals the engine needs.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Ask the shop to inspect the harness and connectors for broken or corroded wires, especially if the problem comes and goes with weather or movement.

issues.t: Spark plug tube seals leak oil and cause misfires on the 2.4L
issues.sym: Rough running, a misfire or check engine light, poor fuel economy, and oil on the spark plugs.
issues.why: The seals around the spark plug tubes fail and let engine oil fill the tubes, fouling the plugs and coils.
issues.next: Have the tubes checked for oil when plugs are changed. Replace the seals and any oil-soaked plugs.

issues.t: Oil pressure light flickers at idle from a bad sender
issues.sym: The oil pressure light comes on at idle even though the oil level is fine and the engine sounds normal.
issues.why: Oil seeps through the oil pressure sending unit and shorts it, giving a false warning.
issues.next: Check the oil level first. If the engine is quiet and the level is good, a shop can test real oil pressure and replace the sender.

issues.t: EGR valve or passage clogs on the 2.5L V6
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough idle or hesitation.
issues.why: The pipe that feeds exhaust gas back to the intake fills with oily soot, so the EGR valve stops working.
issues.next: Have the EGR valve and its pipe cleaned or replaced. The valve and its transducer are sold as a matched set.

issues.t: Blower fan only works on high or not at all
issues.sym: The heater/A/C fan only runs on the highest speed, or stops on all speeds unless you wiggle the fan switch.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor fails, and the fan switch itself can also wear out.
issues.next: Start with the blower resistor, which is a simple fix. If that doesn't last, replace the fan switch too.

issues.t: Horn sounds by itself
issues.sym: The horn blows on its own while driving or parked.
issues.why: Plastic insulators in the horn contact plate under the airbag wear out, letting the horn circuit short to ground.
issues.next: Pull the horn relay or fuse as a temporary fix. Airbag removal is needed to repair the contact plate, so leave it to a shop.

issues.t: ABS warning light from a corroded power distribution center
issues.sym: The ABS light stays on and anti-lock braking stops working. Normal brakes still work.
issues.why: Corrosion in the power distribution center (main fuse and relay box) cuts power to the ABS system.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read and the fuse box checked for corrosion. Parts may be hard to find, so ask about used or repaired units.

issues.t: Power steering hose can leak and catch fire (recall 06V-001)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking onto the engine, smoke from under the hood, a squealing belt, or steering that suddenly gets heavy. Some cars caught fire.
issues.why: The high-pressure power steering hose can leak fluid onto hot engine parts.
issues.next: If you see smoke, pull over and shut off the engine. Check your VIN for this recall; a dealer replaces the hose for free.

issues.t: Cylinder head oil plug can leak and start a fire (recall 96V-006)
issues.sym: Oil leaking at the engine and a burning smell or smoke.
issues.why: A plug in the engine was not sealed and held in well enough, so it can leak oil onto hot parts.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for this recall and have it done at a dealer for free.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can leak (recall 96V-075)
issues.sym: The brake warning light comes on and the pedal feels softer, with longer stops.
issues.why: Brake fluid can leak from the master cylinder, cutting braking on half of the system.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for this recall. Don't drive with a brake warning light on.

issues.t: ABS valve can stick and make the car swerve (recall 96V-074)
issues.sym: The car pulls or swerves to one side during a straight stop.
issues.why: Corrosion in the ABS hydraulic unit can make a front wheel valve stick.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it done for free at a dealer.

issues.t: Hood may not stay latched (recall 97V-095)
issues.sym: The hood can fly up while driving if the main latch isn't engaged.
issues.why: The secondary hood latch can catch without the main latch, leaving the hood unsecured.
issues.next: Make sure the hood is fully closed. Check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Lower control arm ball joint can separate (recall 97V-201)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end and loose steering. If the ball joint comes apart, the wheel can collapse.
issues.why: The lower control arm ball joint can separate from the arm.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Have any front-end clunk inspected right away.

issues.t: Key-shift interlock can stop working (recall 98V-183)
issues.sym: The shifter can be moved out of Park without the key, or the key can come out when not in Park.
issues.why: The ignition-park interlock that ties the key to the shifter can fail.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Car can roll away after being shifted to Park (recall 04V-021)
issues.sym: The car may not be fully held in Park and can roll, especially if the parking brake isn't set.
issues.why: A fault in the floor shifter's ignition-park interlock can let the car be left out of Park.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time you park. Check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Rear brake lines can leak (recall 99V-244)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leaking near a rear wheel, a soft pedal or longer stopping distances.
issues.why: A rear brake tube can leak, cutting braking on half of the system.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for this recall and have any brake fluid leak fixed right away.

issues.t: Front brake line bracket can break (recall 00V-196)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a brake line leaks; then the pedal goes soft.
issues.why: A bracket weld can separate and let the right front brake line fatigue and crack.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Child seat anchors may not hold (recall 00V-366)
issues.sym: No symptom. A child seat attached to the anchors may not stay secured in a crash.
issues.why: The child seat anchorages didn't meet the federal strength standard.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall before using the anchors.

issues.t: Child lock labels may be wrong (recall 00V-066)
issues.sym: The rear door child-lock label may show the wrong position, so you may think it is on when it is off.
issues.why: Incorrect labels were installed.
issues.next: Test the rear doors from the inside to confirm the child lock works, and check your VIN for this recall.
